title: Flat base change of quasi-coherent direct image from an algebraic space
statement: Let $S,T,T'$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $f:X\to T$ be a quasi-compact separated morphism from an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space, lem-trf-space-qc-separated-etale-local], and let $g:T'\to T$ be a flat $S$-morphism [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Put $X'=X\times_TT'$, with projections $h:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to T'$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Let $M$ be a quasi-coherent module on $(X_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal O_X)$ [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Use the canonical ringed etale topoi [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model] and their tensor pullback and direct image functors [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Then the canonical base-change morphism $\beta_M:g^*f_*M\to f'_*h^*M$ is an isomorphism. Here $\beta_M$ is the adjoint, under $f'^*\dashv f'_*$, of the composite $f'^*g^*f_*M\simeq h^*f^*f_*M\xrightarrow{h^*\epsilon_M}h^*M$, where $\epsilon_M$ is the pullback/direct-image counit. The comparison is natural in $M$. No finite-presentation, coherence, properness, or Noetherian hypothesis is required.

source.place: Tag 073K (lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology), clause (1) for i=0, with f separated hence quasi-separated; the canonical map is the ordinary degree-zero adjunction base-change map. The flatness/site comparison used there is spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 073C (lemma-flat-morphism-sites).

proof.text: Set $N=f_*M$. It is quasi-coherent by [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-quasi-coherent-pushforward]. Cover $T$ by affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$, and each $g^{-1}V$ by affine opens $W=\operatorname{Spec}B$, using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. To test the map over $W$, use every affine etale scheme $Z=\operatorname{Spec}D\to W$. Such objects cover every object of the small etale site: cover that scheme by affine opens. Thus it suffices to show the component of $\beta_M$ on each such $Z$ is bijective. This sufficiency is the sheaf axiom: local inverses of a fixed morphism agree on overlaps by uniqueness and glue. The ring map $A\to B$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion], $B\to D$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat], and hence $A\to D$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-comp].

Fix $V,W,Z$ as above. Write $X_V=X\times_TV$ and $M_V=M|_{X_V}$. Etale localization [lem-trf-space-etale-module-pushforward-restriction] identifies $N|_V$ with $(f_V)_*M_V$ and identifies etale tensor pullbacks with restrictions. The definition of quasi-compactness in [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-etale-local], applied to $V\to T$, supplies a quasi-compact scheme atlas of $X_V$; separation is inherited because its diagonal is a scheme test of the closed diagonal of $f$. Refine that atlas by [lem-trf-space-qc-finite-affine-atlas-refinement] to a surjective etale map $p:U\to X_V$ with $U$ affine. By [lem-trf-space-separated-affine-chart-overlap], $R=U\times_{X_V}U$ is affine, with etale projections $p_1,p_2$, and the scheme maps $a:U\to V$ and $b:R\to V$ are quasi-compact separated.

source.place: Tags 03M8 (lemma-compute-pushforward), 03M9 (lemma-pushforward), affine atlas and relation; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03H6 (lemma-quasi-compact-affine-cover).

proof.text: Put $M_U=p^*M_V$, $M_R=p_1^*M_U$, $P=\Gamma(U,M_U)$ and $Q=\Gamma(R,M_R)$. These restrictions are quasi-coherent: etale restriction restricts the local presentations defining quasi-coherence. By [lem-trf-space-pushforward-atlas-equalizer], evaluating its kernel at the final object $V$ gives $N(V)=K:=\ker(\delta:P\to Q)$, where $\delta(s)=p_1^*s-p_2^*s$ with the canonical descent identification on $R$. Kernels of sheaves of modules are evaluated objectwise: the objectwise kernel satisfies the sheaf axiom since the two compatible families can be glued and equality can be tested locally. Thus this is an equality of the specified $A$-module section maps, not just an abstract identification.

source.place: Tag 03M8 (lemma-compute-pushforward), displayed kernel sequence and proof.

proof.text: Base-change the atlas to $X_Z=X_V\times_VZ$. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], $U_D=U\times_VZ\to X_Z$ is a surjective etale atlas; its relation is $R_D=R\times_VZ$ by associativity of fibre products (both represent triples with the same images). The affine-spectrum fibre-product formula [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] makes $U_D$ and $R_D$ affine. Let $M_Z$ be the pullback of $M_V$ to $X_Z$. Pullback preserves quasi-coherence by [lem-sfb-space-module-pullback-quasicoherent]. Applying the atlas equalizer to $M_Z$ now gives $\Gamma(X_Z,M_Z)=\ker(\delta_D:\Gamma(U_D,M_Z|_{U_D})\to\Gamma(R_D,M_Z|_{R_D}))$. Here sections over $X_Z$ mean the canonical compatible chart sections, so the equality is precisely the final-object evaluation of that node.

source.place: Tag 03M8 after base change; spaces-cohomology.tex Tag 073K, affine base-change setup.

proof.text: The scheme Zariski/etale equivalence [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] identifies $M_U,M_R$ with ordinary quasi-coherent modules, identifies their pullbacks with etale tensor pullback, and is the identity on open sections. Apply [lem-pc-flat-affine-base-change-sections] to the whole affine open $U$ of $U\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, and likewise to $R$. It gives isomorphisms $D\otimes_AP\simeq\Gamma(U_D,M_Z|_{U_D})$ and $D\otimes_AQ\simeq\Gamma(R_D,M_Z|_{R_D})$, each sending $d\otimes s$ to $d\,q^*s$, where $q$ is the appropriate projection. The identifications of the modules here follow from associativity of tensor pullback in the two cartesian paths: on tensors it sends $c\otimes(e\otimes m)$ to $ce\otimes m$, with inverse $c\otimes m\mapsto c\otimes(1\otimes m)$. Under these isomorphisms, the two restriction maps agree with $1_D\otimes p_i^*$: both send $d\otimes s$ to $d\,q_R^*(p_i^*s)$. The equality is checked on pure tensors, which generate the tensor product. Consequently $\delta_D$ is $1_D\otimes\delta$.

source.place: Tags 01I9 (lemma-widetilde-pullback) and 01IA (lemma-quasi-coherent-affine); coherent.tex Tag 02KG (lemma-affine-base-change); descent.tex Tag 03LC (proposition-equivalence-quasi-coherent-functorial).

proof.text: Tensor the exact sequence $0\to K\to P\xrightarrow{\delta}Q$ with the flat $A$-algebra $D$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact], $D\otimes_AK\to D\otimes_AP$ is injective and its image is exactly $\ker(1_D\otimes\delta)$. Therefore Steps 3--5 give a bijective map $\theta_D:D\otimes_AN(V)\to\Gamma(X_Z,M_Z)$: the image of $d\otimes s$ has atlas restriction $d\,q_U^*(s|_U)$. This proves bijectivity by the actual kernel diagrams; it does not assume that scalar extension commutes with an arbitrary limit.

source.place: Tag 00HD (lemma-flat), exactness of flat tensor; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03M8 kernel diagram.

proof.text: Identify the source component. The Zariski/etale equivalence and its functorial pullback comparison take $N|_V$ to the ordinary quasi-coherent module with the same sections. The affine pullback-section formula [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections], first for $W\to V$ and then for $Z\to W$, gives $(g^*N)(Z)\simeq D\otimes_B(B\otimes_AN(V))\simeq D\otimes_AN(V)$. The last isomorphism sends $d\otimes(b\otimes s)$ to $db\otimes s$ and has inverse $d\otimes s\mapsto d\otimes(1\otimes s)$. Etale direct-image restriction identifies the target component $(f'_*h^*M)(Z)$ with $\Gamma(X_Z,M_Z)$. These comparisons all use the prescribed adjunction units and the given structure ring maps.

Under Step 7, the specified mate $\beta_M$ is $\theta_D$. Indeed, the counit $f^*f_*M\to M$ evaluates a direct-image section on its chart: this follows from the chart projections and unit formula in [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], by the adjunction triangle identity. Thus the adjoint composite in the statement sends $d\otimes s$, after restriction to $U_D$, to $d\,q_U^*(s|_U)$. This is exactly the atlas restriction of $\theta_D(d\otimes s)$ in Step 6. Restriction from $\Gamma(X_Z,M_Z)$ to its atlas is injective by the equalizer of Step 4, so the two maps agree on pure tensors and hence agree. All components on the covering affine etale tests are therefore bijective. Their inverses glue as in Step 1, proving that $\beta_M$ is an isomorphism. For a module map $t:M\to\widetilde M$, both paths in the naturality square send $d\otimes s$ on $U_D$ to $d\,q_U^*(t_U(s|_U))$; atlas injectivity proves naturality. No finiteness condition on $M$ or on the rings was used.

Edge cases hold (X empty with Spec 0, M=0, g=id, f affine, infinite-rank M). lean.note: The canonical base-change transformation is the adjoint, via the prescribed moduleTensorAdjunction, of the tensor-normalized square comparison followed by the prescribed counit. Supporting declarations construct that comparison from uniquely specified tensor associativity, with the actual chart scalar maps. The main theorem states that its component is invertible for a quasi-coherent module, with scheme targets, flat base map and quasi-compact separated source map. A sheaf pullback square with its projections encodes X-prime = X times_T T-prime without choosing an arbitrary comparison map; naturality is built into the transformation.
